overview: A Pacific storm track keeps the West busy through the holiday weekend. The Cascades and Coast Mountains get the first round Wednesday into Thursday, then a weaker system follows Friday. Wyoming and Colorado get snow mainly from Friday night through Saturday as northwest flow sets up.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A warm front and then a cold front cross Washington Wednesday night through Thursday, bringing rain and snow to the passes, with winds strongest along the coast and northern interior. Snow follows Friday. Crystal Mountain leads with 24" total, and the NWS is calling for more, 20 to 39 inches Wednesday night through Monday night. A Winter Storm Warning runs for Mt. Baker from Wednesday night to Friday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Warm, wet air brings mostly rain to the Coast Mountains through Thursday and Friday, with a snow line that stays high. Whistler's 30" total comes mostly from Wednesday's heavy rain and snow. Cypress Mountain sees rain Wednesday and Thursday with strong southerly winds, and its best snow arrives Monday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Dry, mild weather holds through Thanksgiving. A Pacific system brings snow to western Wyoming Thursday night and Friday, then a stronger wave Friday night into Saturday brings strong westerly wind. Jackson Hole leads with 16" total, and the NWS is calling for more, 15 to 28 inches Thursday night through Monday night. Grand Targhee's total is 15" with an NWS forecast of 21 to 40 inches.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Mild and wet weather dominates through Thursday, with rain falling on lower slopes and the snow level around 1500 metres. Snow chances return Sunday and Monday as colder air arrives. Whitewater has the most at 10" total, with its biggest day Monday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Mild and dry weather holds through Thanksgiving. Northwest flow brings snow Friday night through Saturday night, favoring the Park Range and northern Colorado mountains. Steamboat leads with 9" total, and the NWS is calling for more, 8 to 17 inches Friday night through Monday night. Snow spreads south toward Vail with lighter amounts.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says the Pacific Northwest and northern Rockies will see another round of heavy precipitation around Tuesday Dec 1 and into the following days, with snow in the mountains and rain on the coast.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
